body:
Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust has agreed to acquire a 75.1% stake in a $5 billion portfolio of Amazon data centres, with approximately $2.5 billion in mortgage financing planned for the transaction. Announced on 16 November 2026, the deal covers 13 facilities in Indiana and Mississippi, which Amazon will continue to occupy under long-term leases while retaining a 24.9% ownership interest.

Blackstone expects to contribute approximately $1.9 billion from its initial public offering, while Amazon’s retained stake is valued at around $600 million. The portfolio carries an initial capitalisation rate of 7%, implying approximately $350 million in annual property net operating income before financing costs, although that figure does not represent the cash return available to Blackstone investors.

Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust (BXDC) signed the agreement on 11 November 2026 to acquire a 75.1% controlling interest in two joint ventures with Amazon Data Services affiliates. Amazon will retain the remaining 24.9%, while the joint ventures will hold two data centre campuses comprising 13 newly constructed facilities.

The portfolio includes nine buildings in northern Indiana, within the greater Chicago data centre market, and four in Mississippi. Together, the properties have approximately 647 megawatts of aggregate information technology power capacity, according to BXDC’s 16 November SEC filing.

The $5 billion figure represents the gross value of the underlying properties, rather than a cash payment by BXDC for its majority interest. The transaction would be the investment trust’s first acquisition following its stock market listing earlier in 2026.

Completion is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to closing conditions. The ownership transfer and associated mortgage borrowing had not been completed when the transaction was announced.

BXDC expects to invest approximately $1.9 billion of cash raised through its initial public offering. A further $2.5 billion is expected to come from new non-recourse mortgage loans secured against the data centres, with the borrowing incurred by subsidiaries of the property-owning joint ventures.

Amazon’s retained 24.9% ownership interest is valued at approximately $600 million. The three disclosed figures — $1.9 billion in BXDC cash, $2.5 billion in planned debt and $600 million in retained Amazon equity — reconcile to the portfolio’s approximately $5 billion gross valuation, although the final funding arrangements remain subject to adjustments and transaction costs.

Under the agreement, Amazon will contribute the properties to the joint ventures and receive both its retained minority interest and a cash distribution at closing. The distribution is expected to be funded through BXDC’s cash contribution and the net proceeds of the mortgage loans, rather than through a separate $5 billion payment by Blackstone.

The funding amounts should not be confused with the joint ventures’ ownership percentages. BXDC will hold 75.1% of the equity, while Amazon will retain 24.9%; the $2.5 billion mortgage borrowing represents debt owed by the property-owning entities, not an additional ownership stake.

The lenders have provided debt commitment letters, subject to specified conditions. Non-recourse financing generally limits recovery to the relevant borrowing entities and pledged collateral, subject to contractual exceptions, but the properties’ income will still need to support their debt obligations.

BXDC has disclosed an initial capitalisation rate of 7% for the portfolio. In commercial property investment, this measure compares annual net operating income with the value of the underlying real estate, before financing costs.

Applying that rate to the approximately $5 billion valuation gives implied annual property net operating income of approximately $350 million. The calculation provides a measure of the income associated with the transaction’s valuation, but it is not a reported profit figure or an estimate of cash that BXDC shareholders will receive.

The distinction matters because the proposed mortgage loans will introduce interest expenses and **other financing obligations.** Property net operating income is measured before debt service, so the amount ultimately available to equity investors will depend on borrowing costs, other expenses and the allocation of cash between the joint-venture partners.

The disclosed 7% rate also reflects the initial transaction valuation rather than a guaranteed investment return. The eventual financial results will depend on the properties’ performance and the final financing terms after completion.

Amazon Data Services will lease the entire portfolio under long-term, triple-net arrangements, with a weighted-average initial lease term of 12 years and a weighted-average fully extended term of 32 years. The leases include annual rent increases of 2.75%, while Amazon.com will guarantee the tenant’s payment obligations.

Under a triple-net lease, the tenant generally bears specified property operating expenses in addition to rent. This structure can reduce the landlord’s direct exposure to certain running costs, although the precise responsibilities depend on the lease agreements.

The annual rent increases provide a contractual mechanism for rental income to rise over time. They do not establish the eventual return on BXDC’s investment, which will also reflect debt servicing, management expenses and other financial obligations.

The arrangement gives the joint ventures a single corporate tenant group across both campuses. Although the leases provide long-term contracted occupancy, the concentration means the portfolio’s rental income will depend heavily on Amazon’s continued performance of its contractual obligations.

The acquisition is expected to close before the end of 2026, subject to financing and other conditions. Under the contribution agreement, either party may have the right to terminate the transaction if it has not closed by 31 December, although the agreement allows for an extension in certain circumstances.

A $150 million termination fee may become payable if a party fails to complete the transaction under specified conditions. The fee is not an existing liability and would only apply if the relevant contractual requirements are met.

BXDC’s September 2026 quarterly filing also identifies risks arising from the portfolio’s reliance on Amazon as its sole tenant group and its concentration across two data centre campuses. The final mortgage terms have yet to be established, leaving the borrowing costs associated with the acquisition uncertain until financing is completed.
